residue.text: Source-bound deferred concern: one miswrite is stipulated; repeated mismatch-triggered refresh feedback is unobserved. The supplied diagnostic proposal crosses changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding under matched initial states and actions. Predicted recurrence requires a return refresh to change a retained selection; an extra refresh alone is insufficient. Diagnostic arms may violate the unchanged no-wrong-write outcome.

Source-bound deferred interventions from the concerns remain hypotheses: suppress mismatch-triggered refreshes using equal-duration inspection slots, or inject/withhold mismatch notifications at matched request gates. Log requests separately from actual writes, retaining ordinary schedules, final freshness and the ten-minute ceiling. These proposals distinguish mismatch-to-refresh from refresh-to-mismatch; neither establishes a repeating loop or observed success.

Source-bound unresolved limits: real selection binding, detection rates and interruption costs are unknown; concurrency, deleted keys and snapshot-load failures are excluded. Production connectors, macros, collaboration telemetry and usability participants are unavailable. Equal scores do not identify targets. summary.text: Retain the stage1 selection-reordering account: the supplied trace stipulates refresh changing the key at a retained row, followed by a wrong-target commit. General causal sufficiency remains a hypothesis. The concerns question necessity of refresh before every commit because only final freshness is mandatory; no completed correction trace is supplied.

Proposed construction: keep S0 loaded. Inspect/select K2 during minutes 0-1, commit during 1-2; inspect/select K5 during 2-3, commit during 3-4; inspect/select K7 during 4-5, commit during 5-6. Refresh only during 6-7. This omits the challenged dependency without intermediate refreshes or correction loops.

Prospective hypothesis: stable S0 rows 2, 5 and 7 yield writes only to K2, K5 and K7. Final refresh should load S2 and preserve local statuses by key: exactly those three checked, five unchecked, source scores read-only. Verified seven-minute success would falsify intermediate-refresh necessity within this model; it has not been observed.

Require action times, snapshots, selected rows, intended keys and every actual write. Acceptance requires zero incorrect-key writes even if repaired, exactly three target corrections, unchanged source scores, latest S2 loaded and completion within ten minutes. Inspect immutable keys for final verification: K5 and K7 both score 75, so score-only identification is ambiguous. Any violation rejects the proposed construction.
